ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The gray tile in <image1> is composed of 4 unit squares: there are 3 squares arranged in a row on top, and there is 1 square below connected under the middle square, so it is a T-shaped tetromino. The rectangular grid in <image2> has 5 columns and 4 rows, for a total of 20 unit squares. Reasoning: First look by area, at most only 20/4 = 5 pieces can be placed. Color the 5×4 rectangle like a chessboard. Because there are 20 squares in total and the numbers of rows and columns are 5 and 4, there are 10 black squares and 10 white squares. A T-shaped tetromino in any orientation will cover 3 squares of one color and 1 square of the other color in the chessboard coloring, so the color difference of each tile is ±2. If 5 pieces are placed, they must exactly cover all 20 squares, and at this time the total color difference should be 0; but the sum of five ±2 cannot obtain 0, so 5 pieces is impossible. Next explain that 4 pieces can be done: number the rows from top to bottom 1 to 4, and the columns from left to right 1 to 5, and they can be placed at {(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,2)}, {(1,5),(2,5),(3,5),(2,4)}, {(2,1),(3,1),(4,1),(3,2)}, {(4,3),(4,4),(4,5),(3,4)}. These four groups are all inside the 5×4 rectangle, and are pairwise non-overlapping, and each group is a rotation of the T-shaped tile in the figure. Therefore the maximum number is 4.

raw_record.question_text: Anne has a few grey tiles like the one in the picture. What is the maximum number of these tiles that she can place on the $5 \times 4$ rectangle without any overlaps?

method.method_draft: First read the picture: the grey tile is a T-tetromino made of 4 unit squares, with 3 squares in a row and 1 square attached below the middle square; the board shown is a 5-by-4 grid of 20 unit squares. Use a checkerboard coloring of the 5 by 4 rectangle. Each T-tetromino, in any rotation, covers 3 squares of one checkerboard color and 1 square of the other, so it has color imbalance 2. Since the 5 by 4 rectangle has 10 squares of each color, five tiles would have to cover all 20 squares with total color imbalance 0, but the sum of five imbalances each equal to ±2 cannot be 0. Therefore 5 tiles are impossible, so at most 4 can fit. Then show 4 are possible by giving an explicit placement, for example with rows 1–4 from top to bottom and columns 1–5 from left to right: place tiles on {(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,2)}, {(1,5),(2,5),(3,5),(2,4)}, {(2,1),(3,1),(4,1),(3,2)}, and {(4,3),(4,4),(4,5),(3,4)}. These four placements are non-overlapping, so the maximum is 4.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：<image1> 中的灰色瓷砖由 4 个单位正方形组成：上面有 3 个正方形排成一行，下面有 1 个正方形接在中间正方形的下方，所以它是一个 T 形四连方。<image2> 中的矩形网格有 5 列、4 行，共 20 个单位正方形。推理：先用面积看，最多只能放 20/4 = 5 块。给 5×4 矩形作棋盘染色，因为共有 20 格且行列数为 5 和 4，所以黑白各 10 格。任意方向的 T 形四连方在棋盘染色中都会覆盖一种颜色 3 格、另一种颜色 1 格，因此每块瓷砖的颜色差为 ±2。如果放 5 块，就必须正好覆盖全部 20 格，此时总颜色差应为 0；但 5 个 ±2 相加不可能得到 0，所以 5 块不可能。接着说明 4 块可以做到：把行从上到下编号 1 到 4，列从左到右编号 1 到 5，可放在 {(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,2)}、{(1,5),(2,5),(3,5),(2,4)}、{(2,1),(3,1),(4,1),(3,2)}、{(4,3),(4,4),(4,5),(3,4)}。这四组都在 5×4 矩形内，且两两不重叠，每组都是图中的 T 形瓷砖的一个旋转。因此最大数量是 4。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply checkerboard coloring: every T-tetromino covers 3 squares of one color and 1 of the other, while the 5 by 4 rectangle has equal numbers of black and white squares. Use coordinate placement to verify attainability of 4.
